about: The rules of the whole-fight engine that live only in prose. tools/kb_rules.py joins them with the rules it reads from clocks.json, afflictions.json, venoms.yaml, the curing priorities and ACTIVE_CURE_BLOCKERS, and writes kb/sim/rules.json and rules.md. Tags: MEASURED (counted from log rows), READ (stated in a file or the code), WIKI (the wiki only), PLAYER (a player said so), ASSUMED (nothing supports it yet). Every ASSUMED, PLAYER and WIKI rule has alternatives, so a sweep can run each one. Sources are 1-based editor lines.

rules.source: kb/sim/events.json race[]: the delay of each DSTAB whose 'down' is false (az 9, Z5 5, g 2, X 7)
rules.note: the SSC delay when an affliction lands on an OPEN channel: the strike to the first eat before the next attack, for a DSTAB that found the eat up (a PHASE of 0 takes its sign from the row order, kb_events.phase_at). Per log: az 0.104 (n=9), Z5 0.094 (n=5), g 0.106 (n=2), X 0.120 (n=7). It holds the logger's own reaction too, not a pure SSC delay (kb/sim/events.md). One row with no eat clock known (g 126, down null, 0.018) is in neither case. The engine draws it by rule draw.shape and holds it at 0.001 s or more (victim.lua V.delay). It replaces ssc.delay (0.10-0.18 uniform, two logs' 'may eat' to eat, foundations.md:192), which ran for both cases. The alternative is one opponent's, seen from our seat: rule ssc.delay.gain.Saibel (--ssc-gain saibel), never the default. tools/test_kb_rules.py re-derives it

rules.source: kb/sim/events.json race[]: the delay of each DSTAB whose 'down' is true (az 27, Z5 38, g 20, X 78)
rules.note: the SSC delay when a channel comes back with an affliction WAITING: the eat's return line to the first eat before the next attack, for a DSTAB that found the eat down. Per log: az 0.157, Z5 0.175, g 0.158, X 0.100. The engine also uses it when the affliction that shut a channel is cured (the tree after paralysis); no log measures that case, so there it is ASSUMED by analogy. A 0.000 is a cure in the return's own packet; the engine holds a delay at 0.001 s or more. Saibel's forced eat to eat (n=18, median 1.670, from our seat) fits a clock of about 1.50-1.54 plus a reaction of about 0.16, but our seat cannot see her recovery, so no per-opponent alternative is given (lens TC5). tools/test_kb_rules.py re-derives it

ONE opponent's open-channel reaction, seen from our seat (the 2026-11-07 spar): our paralysis line ('Horror overcomes Saibel's face') to her next magnesium eat, at each landing that came 1.506 s or more after her last herb (her shortest herb eat-to-eat; potash is moss, on its own clock) or before her first. All 9 landings that pass that cut are here, 0.005-0.216: 8 of them within 0.064 s, and FL 1098-1105 at 0.216. The cut is the only selection. Five landings came inside her forced herb eat-to-eat (1.506-1.759, n=18): FL 1462 at 1.514 s after her last herb, FL 999 at 1.530, FL 1141 at 1.566, FL 771 at 1.600 and FL 1098 at 1.610. So for each of them her eat may still have been down, and the delay a return. Which one was is not known. A per-opponent ALTERNATIVE to ssc.delay.gain, swept with --ssc-gain saibel, never a default: 'eat up' is inferred, because our seat cannot see her recovery, and the holdout waits for a victim-seat log (plan, Holdout). n=9, so it is swept min..max. tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

rules.value: quantiles: linear between lo, p10, median, p90 and hi, 10% of the draws in each tail; lo and hi are one p10-p90 width past p10 and p90, held inside min and max
alt: normal: the median +/- 3 sd (three uniform draws), held inside min and max
rules.note: the shape of a drawn clock; --median takes the median and draws nothing, except in a fork: there a clock already running (a channel down at the row, a FLAY of the shield, a smoke for rebounding, an apply of the coating) takes the median of the part of its spread above the time already run, and that part rests on this shape (review R3-engine-2). The --seeds runs of a --median page draw too. A log's min and max are often a lost line or a slowing affliction (clock.rebounding: 0.026 and 250.253 around a median of 8.49; clock.focus max 4.992 against p90 2.542), so a tail never reaches them unless they lie within one width. --clock-draw normal runs the alternative

A named FLAY also takes the coating: rule attack.flay.coating. One that names a defence the target does not have: rule attack.flay.missing

None of the 33 made with it down printed that line. A FLAY that names a defence the target does not have: rule attack.flay.missing. tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

rules.value: coating: a FLAY that names a shield or rebounding the target does not have strips the sileris coating, as a bare FLAY does, and its venom lands
alt: nothing: it strips nothing, and its whip lands with the coating left up (the X 5328 reading)
rules.note: our seat, the 2026-11-07 spar: we sent 'flay Saibel rebounding curare' (FL 283). The game printed 'You try to flay a non-existent aura of rebounding from Saibel.' (FL 305), then 'The protective coating covering the skin of Saibel is ripped away with their protections.' (FL 308), the whip (FL 315) and the paralysis (FL 318), all in one packet. No apply line follows, and our bites met no coating after it. Against it, from a victim's seat: at X 5328 a whip landed with no strip line and the coating stayed up (the snake met it at X 5385), with the shield gone at X 5310 and rebounding at X 5313-5317. That command is not seen, so which defence it named, or whether it was a FLAY of one at all, is not known. One reading of both: a FLAY of a missing rebounding takes the coating and one of a missing shield does not. n=1 each way, so the conflict is open (kb/CONFLICTS.md). The engine runs the value; --flay-missing nothing runs the alternative, and the page prints a FLAY line when a run met the case. tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

rules.value: named
alt: auto: shield, else rebounding, else sileris
rules.note: named follows the wiki's syntax. auto is the engine's own order for a FLAY that names nothing (--flay-order auto): forward.lua has no FLAY of a defence (its strike() turns a shielded DSTAB into a one-venom FLAY)

rules.value: one venom; sileris or fangbarrier blocks it
rules.note: 'BITE <target> [<venom>]' (Venom.wiki:23). Flaying the sileris coating is what lets the fangs sink in again (Subterfuge.wiki:80). The pet's bite meets 'the waxy coating' in all four logs (rule snake lines, kb/sim/events.md)

rules.value: IMPULSE <suggestion> <venom>: it needs the attacker's equilibrium and balance. The suggestion lands, then a bite of the venom (attack.impulse.venom). It spends equilibrium (attack.cost.own.impulse_eq) and the bite's balance. A shield blocks all of it; sileris or fangbarrier blocks the bite only
alt: a shield blocks the bite only
rules.note: the wiki's IMPULSE takes no venom (Hypnosis.wiki:46); our form with a venom is rule attack.impulse.venom. In the spar all 13 were sent with balance and equilibrium both up, so whether it needs both is not tested. No log shows an impulse on a shield or on the coating. The engine refuses an impulse with no venom, or with a suggestion that is not a trivial one (attack.impulse.suggestions). With --gap queue the next action waits attack.cost.own.bite; with a numeric --gap it waits that gap, and a second impulse also waits for the attacker's equilibrium

rules.value: delivers: a bite of the venom comes in the impulse's own packet
rules.note: 13 of 13 impulses ('You craft the impulse of <suggestion> in the mind of <target>.') had 'You sink your fangs into <target>, injecting just the proper amount of <venom>.' 0.000-0.007 s later (median 0.001), and the costs 'Equilibrium used: 1.44s.' and 'Balance used: 1.7s.' after them. This settles the plan's impulse.venom_arg. Equilibrium came back first 13 of 13, so the bite's balance gates the next round (attack.cost.own.impulse_eq, attack.cost.own.bite). tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

the trivial suggestions, the only ones an IMPULSE can give ('one of the trivial suggestions', Hypnosis.wiki:50). The wiki's list (rows 86-249) and the package's TRIVIAL_SUGGESTIONS hold the same 15, in the same order. Clumsiness is a complex suggestion (Hypnosis.wiki:252-254), not a trivial one. The game says 'known to you': which ones this character knows (AB HYPNOSIS) is not captured. The engine refuses an impulse of any other word (tools/sim/attackers.lua A.parse). The spar used four of them: masochism 7, confusion 3, stupidity 2, recklessness 1. tools/test_kb_rules.py checks both lists

the conditions are our own table's (relayed notes, PLAYER); the game's EKANELIA STUDY MONKSHOOD text is not captured. The engine fires it on a BITE, or on the bite of an impulse, when all three are up as the bite lands ('Reactions fire on the bite command', Venom.wiki:391); an impulse of masochism brings the third. The venom's own disloyalty lands too. A DSTAB fires no reaction. What the spar saw: rule reaction.monkshood.seen

rules.value: 8 of 10 monkshood bites fired the reaction: 'You sense the weakness in <target> as your monkshood takes hold.', then her impatience line
rules.note: all 7 masochism impulses fired it (FL 1275, 1324, 1551, 1596, 1643, 1943, 2033), each with 'Saibel shuffles her feet in boredom.' after it. Of the 2 confusion impulses, FL 1693 fired it and FL 1364 did not; the stupidity impulse at FL 1741 did not. our seat, the 2026-11-07 spar. From 'Balance used: 1.8s.' in the DSTAB's packet to the next 'You have recovered balance on all limbs.'; printed 1.8, stated 2.80 (Subterfuge/Doublestab). The median is 1.6335 (the middle pair 1.626 and 1.641); the sd is p90-p10 over 2.563, and the population sd is 0.061. The alt 1.75 (n=24) times the same recovery from the round's first reply ('[System]: Queued freestand commands cleared.'). Each attack.cost.own rule holds its first-reply value in the field first_reply too, and theorycraft --gap queue-late runs those values. Every cost line came in the round's second packet, about 0.09 s after the first reply, and where that step happens (our side or the server's) is open: it decides which of the two the server counts. From the cost line, 21 of the 52 cost lines in this log are within +-0.15 s of their printed value; from the first reply, 50 of 52. An input about our seat, not a refit (plan, Holdout). tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

rules.note: our seat as played on 2026-11-07: raw rounds, one key press per round. Land to land: the strike line of each attack ('You quickly prick', 'You craft the impulse', 'You try to flay') to the next one, the pinshot opener left out. After a DSTAB 1.977 (n=24), after an IMPULSE 1.925 (n=12), after the FLAY 1.773. The spread is skewed (population sd 0.189), so draw.shape's quantiles fit it and a symmetric noise does not. Not usable (p90-p10 0.287, over 0.2): a gap is a choice as well as a cost. Alt 1.634 is the server-queue floor: our DSTAB cost (attack.cost.own.dstab), if a queued round fires as recovery arrives. Alt 1.83 is other Serpents' median (attack.gap.others.dstab). Our seat only: no Saibel number is a victim input. theorycraft --gap raw runs its median before every action (a drawn run adds the --gap-sd noise, not these quantiles); a numeric --gap does not read it. tools/test_kb_rules.py re-counts it

the symmetric noise a drawn run adds to the gap (--gap-sd, default 0.09). 0.09 comes from a printed cost against its measured recovery (foundations.md:116: 89% within +-0.15 s, n=264). It is not a measure of our gap. On our Serpent seat the DSTAB cost line to recovery has a population sd of 0.061 (n=24, attack.cost.own.dstab), the first alternative. The raw land-to-land gap is skewed (population sd 0.189, n=37), and attack.gap.own holds its quantiles
